title: Reported speech
objectives: I can explain why tenses shift when I retell what someone said, and apply the shift correctly.
I can choose the right reporting verb and the construction it needs: que with the indicative, que with the subjunctive, an infinitive, or se.
I can re-point pronouns and references to time and place so they still fit the person who is retelling.
I can tell the difference between the formal shifted pattern and the colloquial pattern ele falou que vem.
I can summarize conversations, interviews and meetings, and explain why the accents and letters in the words I use are written as they are.

vocabulary.note: Reports a firm, confident statement. The endings -ei and -ou (afirmei, afirmou) end in i and u, which predict stress on the last syllable, so no accent is written.

example.target: O ministro afirmou que os números estavam corretos.
example.source: The minister stated that the figures were correct.

vocabulary.note: The verb of official statements, so the register is formal. The r between two vowels in declarou is the soft tap, not the strong rr of erro.

example.target: A empresa declarou que não tinha conhecimento do problema.
example.source: The company declared that it was not aware of the problem.
example.source_literal: The company declared that not had knowledge of-the problem.

vocabulary.note: Adds to what was already said; it is not the verb for adding numbers, which is somar. The group sc before e is said as one s sound, so the word is a-cre-sen-TAR.

example.target: O diretor acrescentou que haveria uma nova reunião.
example.source: The director added that there would be another meeting.
example.source_literal: The director added that there-would-be a new meeting.

vocabulary.note: Takes que plus a clause (admitiu que tinha errado) or, when the subject is the same, ter plus a participle (admitiu ter errado). The t before i is said [tʃ], like the ch of chip, in most of Brazil.

example.target: Ela admitiu que tinha cometido um erro.
example.source: She admitted that she had made a mistake.
example.source_literal: She admitted that had committed a mistake.

vocabulary.note: Usually to deny: negou que soubesse, negou ter dito isso. Negar-se a plus an infinitive means to refuse. A -gar verb needs gu before e to keep the hard g, so I denied is neguei.

example.target: O jogador negou que tivesse brigado com o técnico.
example.source: The player denied that he had argued with the coach.
example.source_literal: The player denied that had fought with the technician.

vocabulary.note: Looks forward, so the clause that follows is in the conditional or ia plus an infinitive: prometeu que voltaria. With the same subject an infinitive is enough: prometeu voltar. Prometeu is stressed on the last syllable, as the ending u predicts, so no accent is written.

example.target: Ele prometeu que chegaria antes das oito.
example.source: He promised that he would arrive before eight.
example.source_literal: He promised that would-arrive before of-the eight.

vocabulary.note: To give someone notice of something, a warning or just news, before or as it happens. The thing announced follows que: avisou que o voo atrasou. The s between vowels is said z: a-vi-ZAR.

example.target: A companhia aérea avisou que o voo sairia com atraso.
example.source: The airline notified us that the flight would leave late.
example.source_literal: The air company notified that the flight would-leave with delay.

vocabulary.note: To promise with certainty. The g before a is hard: ga-ran-TIR, stressed on the last syllable as the ending r predicts.

example.target: O gerente garantiu que o pedido chegaria na quinta-feira.
example.source: The manager guaranteed that the order would arrive on Thursday.
example.source_literal: The manager guaranteed that the order would-arrive in-the fifth-fair.

vocabulary.note: Takes que plus the subjunctive when it proposes an action: sugeriu que fôssemos. The g before e is the zh sound of measure, and the stress is on the last syllable (su-ge-RIR).

example.target: Ela sugeriu que a gente mudasse o horário da reunião.
example.source: She suggested that we change the meeting time.
example.source_literal: She suggested that the people might-change the schedule of-the meeting.

vocabulary.note: To ask for a thing or to ask someone to do something, never to ask a question, which is perguntar. Pedir que takes the subjunctive. Pedir demissão, literally to ask resignation, means to resign. Irregular in the present (eu peço), regular in the preterite (pediu).

example.target: Ela pediu que eu esperasse na recepção.
example.source: She asked me to wait at the reception desk.
example.source_literal: She asked that I might-wait in-the reception.

vocabulary.note: Two meanings, decided by context: to send (mandar um áudio, mandar a ata) and to order (mandou o motorista parar). In the order sense it takes an object plus an infinitive, or que plus the subjunctive. In man, the n closes the syllable and nasalizes the a.

example.target: A chefe mandou todo mundo sair da sala.
example.source: The boss ordered everyone to leave the room.
example.source_literal: The boss sent all world to-leave of-the room.

vocabulary.note: To ask a question; compare pedir, which asks for a thing or an action. Perguntar se introduces a yes or no question, perguntar plus a question word an open one. In per-gun-TAR the u is pronounced; it is silent only in gue and gui.

example.target: Ele perguntou se o voo já tinha chegado.
example.source: He asked whether the flight had already arrived.

vocabulary.note: Insistir que plus an indicative clause insists on a fact (insistiu que não sabia); with the subjunctive it demands (insistiu que eu fosse). The other construction is insistir em plus a noun or infinitive. Stress on the last syllable (in-sis-TIR).

example.target: Ele insistiu que não tinha nada a ver com o caso.
example.source: He insisted that he had nothing to do with the matter.
example.source_literal: He insisted that not had nothing to see with the case.

vocabulary.note: Reclamar que plus a clause reports the complaint; reclamar de plus a noun names its target (reclamou do atendimento, where de plus o gives do).

example.target: Os clientes reclamaram que o atendimento era lento.
example.source: The customers complained that the service was slow.
example.source_literal: The clients complained that the attendance was slow.

vocabulary.note: A close relative of English reveal, with the same meaning. Stress on the last syllable (re-ve-LAR).

example.target: O artista revelou que estava escrevendo um livro.
example.source: The artist revealed that he was writing a book.

vocabulary.note: To make a remark in passing; it need not be a formal opinion. The n in men closes the syllable and nasalizes the e.

example.target: Meu chefe comentou que estava satisfeito com o resultado.
example.source: My boss mentioned that he was satisfied with the result.

vocabulary.note: Re- means again or onward and passar means to pass, so the verb is to pass something on to someone else. The ss between vowels is the s sound; a single s there would be said z.

example.target: Ela repassou a informação para toda a equipe.
example.source: She passed the information on to the whole team.
example.source_literal: She re-passed the information to all the team.

vocabulary.note: From registro, a record: to put something in writing officially. A word-initial r is the strong sound (like the h of hat), although it is written with one r.

example.target: A secretária registrou tudo o que foi decidido.
example.source: The secretary recorded everything that was decided.

vocabulary.note: The same word as the ordinal second (segundo andar) and the unit of time. As a preposition it is followed by a person or a source, never by a verb: segundo a prefeitura, segundo ele.

example.target: Segundo a prefeitura, as obras terminam em março.
example.source: According to city hall, the works end in March.
example.source_literal: Second the city-hall, the works end in March.

vocabulary.note: A formal way to attribute information, or to say that something agrees with a rule: de acordo com a lei. De acordo on its own means in agreement: estou de acordo, I agree.

example.target: De acordo com a ata, a proposta foi aprovada por unanimidade.
example.source: According to the minutes, the proposal was approved unanimously.
example.source_literal: Of accord with the minutes, the proposal was approved by unanimity.

vocabulary.note: A véspera is the day, or the evening, immediately before an event. It is stressed on the third to last syllable (VÉS-pe-ra), so it always carries an accent. Na is em plus a. It is how a report says ontem for a day in the past.

example.target: Ela disse que tinha viajado na véspera.
example.source: She said she had traveled the day before.
example.source_literal: She said that had traveled in-the eve.

vocabulary.note: No is em plus o. In seguinte the u is silent, because g keeps its hard sound before i through a silent u: se-GUIN-te. It replaces amanhã when the reference day is in the past.

example.target: Ele prometeu que voltaria no dia seguinte.
example.source: He promised he would come back the next day.
example.source_literal: He promised that would-return in-the day following.

vocabulary.note: Naquele is em plus aquele written as one word, with n standing for em. It replaces hoje when the reported day is over; naquele momento replaces agora.

example.target: Ele disse que naquele dia ia trabalhar em casa.
example.source: He said he was going to work from home that day.
example.source_literal: He said that in-that day was-going to-work at home.

vocabulary.note: Porta here is a form of the verb portar, to carry, not the noun door: the compound means the one who carries the voice of others. Feminine a porta-voz; plural os porta-vozes. It is stressed on voz, because a word ending in z is stressed on the last syllable by default.

example.target: O porta-voz do clube negou as acusações.
example.source: The club's spokesperson denied the accusations.
example.source_literal: The carry-voice of-the club denied the accusations.

vocabulary.note: Also a fountain, and in Brazil the word for a typeface. In the news, a fonte is the person or document that information comes from: segundo fontes do governo.

example.target: O jornal não revelou a fonte da informação.
example.source: The newspaper did not reveal the source of the information.

vocabulary.note: Unverified information passed from person to person. In bo-A-to the o and a are separate syllables, and the stress falls on a. The plural is boatos.

example.target: Correu um boato de que a fábrica ia fechar.
example.source: A rumor went around that the factory was going to close.
example.source_literal: Ran a rumor of that the factory was-going to-close.

vocabulary.note: A message left with a third person to be passed on, not a conversation. Deixar um recado is to leave a message, dar um recado to pass one on.

example.target: Deixei um recado com a secretária, mas ninguém ligou.
example.source: I left a message with the secretary, but nobody called.

vocabulary.note: The written record of what was said and decided at a meeting. Two syllables, stressed on the first (A-ta) by the default for words ending in a.

example.target: A ata da reunião será enviada por e-mail.
example.source: The minutes of the meeting will be sent by email.

vocabulary.note: In PAU-ta the au is a diphthong, said like the ow of cow. The list of items to discuss at a meeting; in a newsroom, the list of stories to cover.

example.target: O primeiro item da pauta é o orçamento do próximo ano.
example.source: The first item on the agenda is next year's budget.
example.source_literal: The first item of-the agenda is the budget of-the next year.

vocabulary.note: What a meeting decides must happen next, and who takes it forward. From caminho, path: encaminhar is to put something on its path. The n closing en and men nasalizes the vowel, nh is the ny sound, and the stress falls on men (en-ca-mi-nha-MEN-to).

example.target: O encaminhamento da reunião foi contratar dois novos analistas.
example.source: The follow-up from the meeting was to hire two new analysts.
example.source_literal: The putting-on-the-path of-the meeting was to-hire two new analysts.

dialogues.title: Office grapevine
dialogues.context: At the office, Priscila, Marcos and Elaine are passing on a rumor and arguing about exactly what was said.

lines.speaker: Priscila
lines.target: Marcos, você não sabe o que a Elaine me contou hoje de manhã!
lines.source: Marcos, you won't believe what Elaine told me this morning!
lines.source_literal: Marcos, you not know what the Elaine me told today of morning!

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.target: O que foi? Conta logo!
lines.source: What is it? Tell me already!
lines.source_literal: What was-it? Tell soon!

lines.speaker: Priscila
lines.target: Ela disse que o Rodrigo ia pedir demissão no fim do mês.
lines.source: She said that Rodrigo was going to resign at the end of the month.
lines.source_literal: She said that the Rodrigo was-going to-ask resignation in-the end of-the month.

lines.speaker: Elaine
lines.target: Calma, Priscila, eu não falei exatamente isso. Eu disse que tinha ouvido dizer que ele estava procurando outro emprego.

lines.source_literal: Calm, Priscila, I not spoke exactly that. I said that had heard say that he was looking-for another job.

lines.speaker: Marcos

lines.source_literal: To-hear to-say is different of to-have certainty, not-is? Who you spoke that?

lines.source_literal: The Letícia, of-the financial. She told that saw the résumé of-him in-the printer.

lines.speaker: Priscila
lines.target: Então pode ser verdade. Ontem ele me perguntou se eu conhecia alguém numa empresa de tecnologia.

lines.speaker: Marcos
lines.target: Hum, aí fica estranho mesmo. Mas semana passada eu perguntei se estava tudo bem, e ele respondeu que estava ótimo.
lines.source: Hmm, now it really does get strange. But last week I asked if everything was fine, and he answered that he was great.
lines.source_literal: Hmm, there it-becomes strange same. But week passed I asked if was all well, and he answered that was great.

lines.speaker: Elaine
lines.target: As pessoas nem sempre falam a verdade, Marcos. E o chefe, será que já sabe?
lines.source: People don't always tell the truth, Marcos. And the boss, does he know yet?
lines.source_literal: The people not-even always speak the truth, Marcos. And the boss, will-be that already knows?

lines.speaker: Priscila
lines.target: Não sei. Mas eu prometi pra Letícia que não ia contar pra ninguém. Opa.
lines.source: I don't know. But I promised Letícia that I wouldn't tell anyone. Oops.
lines.source_literal: Not I-know. But I promised for Letícia that not was-going to-tell for nobody. Oops.

lines.target: Pois é, agora você já contou pra todo mundo.
lines.source: Well, now you've told everyone.
lines.source_literal: Since it-is, now you already told for all world.

lines.speaker: Elaine
lines.target: Vamos combinar uma coisa: ninguém repassa isso até a gente ter certeza.

lines.source_literal: Let's agree a thing: nobody re-passes this until the people to-have certainty.

dialogues.title: Writing the minutes
dialogues.context: Helena, the secretary, checks with the director, Seu Antônio, and with Vera how to record what was said at yesterday's meeting.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.target: Seu Antônio, estou escrevendo a ata da reunião de ontem. Posso confirmar alguns pontos?
lines.source: Seu Antônio, I'm writing the minutes of yesterday's meeting. May I confirm a few points?
lines.source_literal: Mister Antônio, I-am writing the minutes of-the meeting of yesterday. I-can confirm some points?

lines.speaker: Antônio
lines.target: Claro, Helena. Pode perguntar.
lines.source: Of course, Helena. Go ahead.
lines.source_literal: Clear, Helena. You-can ask.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.target: Logo no início, o senhor declarou que a empresa tinha atingido a meta do trimestre, correto?
lines.source: Right at the start, you declared that the company had reached the quarter's target, correct?
lines.source_literal: Soon in-the beginning, the sir declared that the company had reached the goal of-the quarter, correct?

lines.speaker: Antônio
lines.target: Isso. Eu afirmei que vendemos dez por cento acima do previsto.
lines.source: That's right. I stated that we sold ten percent above the forecast.
lines.source_literal: That. I stated that we-sold ten per cent above of-the foreseen.

lines.speaker: Vera

lines.source: And I suggested that the deadline for the new project be extended by two weeks, remember?
lines.source_literal: And I suggested that the deadline of-the new project might-be extended for two weeks, remember?

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.target: Lembro, Vera. Vou registrar que você sugeriu a extensão. E o senhor respondeu que ia analisar a proposta.
lines.source: I remember, Vera. I'll record that you suggested the extension. And you answered that you would look at the proposal.
lines.source_literal: I-remember, Vera. I-go to-record that you suggested the extension. And the sir answered that was-going to-analyze the proposal.

lines.speaker: Antônio
lines.target: Exato. Pode escrever que eu prometi dar uma resposta até sexta-feira.
lines.source: Exactly. You can write that I promised to give an answer by Friday.
lines.source_literal: Exact. Can write that I promised to-give an answer until sixth-fair.

lines.speaker: Vera
lines.target: E o encaminhamento sobre a contratação? O Jorge perguntou se haveria vagas no próximo semestre.

lines.source_literal: And the putting-on-the-path about the hiring? The Jorge asked if there-would-be vacancies in-the next semester.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.target: Isso. E o senhor disse que a decisão dependeria do orçamento.
lines.source: Yes. And you said that the decision would depend on the budget.
lines.source_literal: That. And the sir said that the decision would-depend of-the budget.

lines.speaker: Antônio
lines.target: Correto. Coloque também que eu pedi que todos enviassem os relatórios até quinta-feira.

lines.source_literal: Correct. Put also that I asked that all might-send the reports until fifth-fair.

lines.speaker: Helena
lines.target: Certo. Vou mandar a ata hoje à tarde para todos os participantes.

dialogues.title: What the chef said on the radio
dialogues.context: Davi heard a radio interview with a famous chef and now retells it to his friends Sofia and Nando.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.target: Davi, você estava ouvindo rádio ontem, né? O que a chef Luíza disse na entrevista?
lines.source: Davi, you were listening to the radio yesterday, right? What did chef Luíza say in the interview?
lines.source_literal: Davi, you were hearing radio yesterday, not-is? What the chef Luíza said in-the interview?

lines.speaker: Davi
lines.target: Disse muita coisa! Primeiro, ela contou que tinha crescido num restaurante de família em Minas.
lines.source: She said a lot! First, she said she had grown up in a family restaurant in Minas.
lines.source_literal: Said much thing! First, she told that had grown in-a restaurant of family in Minas.

lines.speaker: Nando
lines.target: E por que ela saiu de lá?

lines.speaker: Davi

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: stress and accents in the words of this unit
grammar.explanation:
Every accent mark in the words of this unit follows from a few facts about stress, the louder and longer syllable of a word. First, the default: a word that ends in a, e, o, am, em, as, es or os is stressed on the second to last syllable, and a word that ends in i, u, l, r, z or a nasal such as ão, ões, im or um is stressed on the last syllable. A word that obeys its default carries no accent, which is why most words here have none: falou, chegaria, perguntar, porta-voz. Second, an accent appears only when a word breaks its default, and it sits on the stressed vowel. Você ends in e, which predicts the second to last syllable, but the stress is on the last, so an accent is written. Third, a word stressed on the third to last syllable has no default to appeal to, so it is always accented. That is the case of véspera and número, and of the many words ending in -io or -ia, where the course counts the i and the o (or a) as two syllables: re-la-TÓ-ri-o, se-cre-TÁ-ri-a, au-di-ÊN-ci-a.

The mark also tells you the quality of the vowel. The acute accent (á, é, í, ó, ú) marks stress and, on a, e and o, that the vowel is open, as [ɛ] in é or [a] in está; i and u have only one quality, so there it marks stress alone. The circumflex (â, ê, ô) marks stress on a closed vowel, as in [e] in você or [o] in metrô, or on a vowel colored by the nasal consonant that follows it, as in trânsito. The tilde (ã, õ) is not a stress mark on its own: it marks nasality, so irmão is stressed on the last syllable by the default for words ending in ão, and no accent is needed. The grave accent (à, às) is the crase, the fusion of the preposition a with the article a or as, as in à tarde.

Two further cases need their own rule. A stressed one-syllable word that ends in a, e or o, with or without s, is accented: já, lá, é, né, só, nós, mês, três. This separates them from the unstressed little words that carry no stress of their own, such as o, a, de, me, se and que. The second case is a hiatus, two vowels that belong to different syllables. When the second vowel is a stressed i or u it takes an acute: aí is a-Í, two syllables, while ai in pai is one syllable. The mark is not written when that i or u ends the word with a consonant other than s (cair, ruim) or is followed by nh (rainha).

Verb endings obey the same logic. The preterite endings -ei and -ou end in i and u, which predict last-syllable stress, so falei and negou need no accent. The conditional endings -ia and -iam put the stress on the r-i before them, the second to last syllable: chegaria, ligariam, with no accent. Only endings that push the stress to the third to last syllable are accented, such as the nós forms of the imperfect subjunctive: esperássemos, adiássemos. The table applies the same method to the words of this unit: divide into syllables, find the stress, read the default, compare.

rows: Stress third to last, so always accented; open e takes the acute
Same pattern; u has one quality, so the acute marks stress only
Ending -io counts as two syllables, so TÓ is third to last; open o takes the acute
Same pattern; open a takes the acute
Same pattern; the e is closed and nasal before n, so the circumflex
Stress third to last; the a is colored by the following n, so the circumflex
Stress third to last, so accented
Ending e predicts second to last; stress on the last needs an accent; closed e takes the circumflex
Ending em predicts second to last; stress on the last needs an accent
Same as também; the u after g is silent before e
Ending o predicts second to last; stress on the last needs an accent; closed o takes the circumflex
já, lá, só, nós, mês, né
A stressed one-syllable word ending in a, e or o (with or without s) is accented
Stressed i after another vowel in a separate syllable takes the acute; ai without it would be one syllable

grammar.title: Spelling and sound: letters, letter pairs and nasal vowels in the new words
grammar.explanation:
A Portuguese letter does not have one fixed sound; its sound depends on its neighbours and its position in the word. The rules below come from the first lessons, and this note applies them to the new words of this unit.

The letters c and g are hard before a, o, u (k, and g as in go) and soft before e, i (s, and zh as in the s of measure). To write an s sound before a, o, u the cedilla is added: ç, as in almoçado, começou, março and preço. To keep c and g hard before e or i, a silent u is inserted: que, quem, alguém, seguinte, guia. Before a, o or another consonant that u is pronounced: quando and quatro (kw), perguntar. The letter pair sc before e or i is simply one s sound (acrescentar), and the g of gerente, sugerir and regiões is zh because it stands before e or i, while the g of garantir is hard.

Single letters also depend on position. The letter s between two vowels is said z, so to write a true s between vowels Portuguese doubles it: pessoa, isso, disse, impressora. The letter r is strong at the start of a word (relatório, repassar, registrar, reunião) and after n, l or s, and a soft tap between vowels (declarar, prefeitura); to write the strong sound between vowels, rr is used: erro, correu. On its own the letter h is silent: hoje, hora, horário, hotel, haver. It has a sound only inside the pairs ch, lh and nh. The letter x has several values and must be learned with the word: z in the prefix ex before a vowel (exato), s before a consonant (extensão), and s in próximo.

Letter pairs make single sounds: ch is sh (chefe, chegar, fechar), lh is the ly of million (filha, trabalho) and nh is the ny of canyon (minha, estranho, conhecer). Diphthongs, two vowels in one syllable, appear in the past-tense endings (deixei, negou, ligou, jurou), in dois and coisa, and in pauta and audiência. The word muito is said with a nasal ui even though nothing in the spelling shows it.

Nasal sounds come from two sources. A vowel followed by m or n that closes the syllable is nasalized: encaminhamento, ouvindo, também. The tilde marks nasality in ã and õ: mãe, não, irmão, and the plural of most words in -ção or -são is -ções or -sões, with the last syllable stressed and no accent written, as with ão: informação becomes informações, sugestão becomes sugestões, acusação becomes acusações.

grammar.title: What reported speech is, and why the tenses shift
grammar.explanation:
Direct speech quotes the words exactly as they were said, after a colon or in quotation marks: Ela disse: Estou cansada. Reported speech, also called indirect speech, retells the content from the point of view of the person who is speaking now: Ela disse que estava cansada. It has two parts. The reporting verb (disse, perguntou, prometeu) says what kind of speaking took place, and the reported clause (que estava cansada) carries the content. A clause is a group of words built around its own conjugated verb. Here it is joined to the reporting verb by que for statements or by se for yes or no questions, the counterparts of English that and whether.

The principle behind the tense changes is that a tense does not name a time by itself; it places an event relative to a reference moment, normally the moment of speaking. When she said Estou cansada, the present estou meant at this moment. When you retell it a day later, that moment is past, so the content is a state that held at a past moment, and Portuguese uses the imperfect, the tense of past states and backgrounds: estava. Every other tense moves in the same way, one step back from the reporter's present. This is called backshift. English does exactly the same (I am tired becomes she said she was tired; I went becomes she said she had gone; I will come becomes she said she would come), so the logic is familiar and only the forms differ.

Three forms do the work. The present and the present progressive become the imperfect and the imperfect progressive: moro becomes morava, estou trabalhando becomes estava trabalhando. An action before the original moment, whether it was expressed by the preterite (fui) or by the compound past (tenho trabalhado), becomes the pluperfect, the past of a past, which is tinha plus the participle: tinha ido, tinha trabalhado. Here tinha is the imperfect of ter acting as a helper verb exactly as tenho does in the compound past you already know, and the participle (ido, comprado, feito) is the same form and does not change for gender or number. Formal writing often uses havia in place of tinha (havia estudado) with the same meaning, and old-fashioned or literary texts have a one-word pluperfect ending in -ra (falara, declarara, fora) that means the same as tinha plus the participle; you will only meet it in books. The next unit studies the pluperfect fully. The future becomes the conditional, whose Portuguese name, futuro do pretérito, says what it is: a future seen from the past. Chegarei becomes chegaria. The spoken future with ir shifts in the same way: vou chegar becomes ia chegar, the imperfect of ir plus the infinitive.

The mood does not change, only the tense. A clause that already needed the subjunctive keeps it and moves back: the present subjunctive and the future subjunctive both become the imperfect subjunctive (Espero que você venha becomes ela disse que esperava que eu viesse; Quando eu chegar, ligo becomes disse que, quando chegasse, ligaria). The helper-verb pattern repeats in the subjunctive: tinha plus participle in the indicative corresponds to tivesse plus participle in the subjunctive (negou que tivesse lido), where tivesse is the imperfect subjunctive of ter. An imperative becomes the imperfect subjunctive after a request verb, which the next note explains.

Nothing shifts in three cases. If the reporting verb is itself in the present (Ela diz que está cansada) the reporter's moment is still the moment of speaking. An imperfect or a pluperfect in the original has no earlier tense to move to, so it stays (Morava em Recife becomes Disse que morava em Recife). And if the content is still true and the reporter wants to say so, the present can stay: Ele disse que a reunião é amanhã. Everyday speech goes further than this, as the last note shows.

A note on the word-for-word lines in this unit: an imperfect subjunctive is shown with might- (pediu que eu esperasse, asked that I might-wait), because English has no separate verb form for it.

grammar.title: Reporting verbs: the meaning of the verb decides what follows
grammar.explanation:
Dizer, falar and contar are the neutral reporting verbs; they say only that words were spoken. The others add what kind of act the speaking was: afirmar and declarar report a firm or official statement, acrescentar a further remark, comentar a passing one, revelar something disclosed, admitir a concession, negar a rejection, reclamar a complaint, garantir and prometer a commitment, avisar a warning or notice, insistir a repeated claim or demand, sugerir a proposal, pedir a request, mandar an order and perguntar a question. Choosing the precise verb is how a report conveys the way something was said, not only what was said.

The grammar after the verb depends on one question: does the verb present the content as a fact, or as something not yet real? Verbs of statement (dizer, afirmar, declarar, acrescentar, avisar, admitir, reclamar) are followed by que and the indicative, with the tenses shifted as in the previous note: Afirmou que estava pronto. Prometer and garantir look forward, so what follows is the conditional or ia plus the infinitive: Prometeu que ligaria. Requests, suggestions and orders (pedir, sugerir, exigir, which means to demand, and mandar que) describe something wished for that has not happened, which is exactly the job of the subjunctive. Because the reporting verb is in the past, it is the imperfect subjunctive: Pediu que esperássemos. That is also why an imperative in the original (Espere aqui!) becomes an imperfect subjunctive in the report (Pediu que eu esperasse ali). English handles requests with an object and an infinitive (asked me to wait); Portuguese keeps that pattern for mandar (Mandou a gente sair) and, in speech, for pedir para (Pediu pra gente esperar).

Negar presents a claim only in order to reject it, so the speaker does not assert the claim as true, and the subjunctive follows: Negou que soubesse, Negou que tivesse brigado. Some verbs change mood with their meaning. Sugerir meaning to propose takes the subjunctive, but sugerir meaning to indicate takes the indicative: Os números sugerem que a economia está melhorando. Insistir que before a fact is indicative (Insistiu que não sabia de nada); before a demand it is subjunctive (Insistiu que eu fosse). Mandar has two meanings, to send (Mandou um áudio) and to order (Mandou o motorista parar); the context and the infinitive tell them apart.

When the subject of the reporting verb is also the subject of the reported action, Portuguese often replaces the que clause with an infinitive: Prometeu voltar, Admitiu ter errado, Negou ter dito isso. Ter dito is the perfect infinitive, ter plus the participle, the infinitive counterpart of tinha dito.

Questions are reported with perguntar or querer saber, to want to know. A yes or no question has no question word and is introduced by se, whether: Perguntou se eu queria ir. An open question keeps its question word: Perguntou onde eu morava. Keep pedir and perguntar apart: asking for a thing or an action is pedir, asking for information is perguntar.

grammar.title: Pronouns, time and place words, and indirect questions
grammar.explanation:
Some words do not carry their meaning on their own; they point at the situation of whoever is speaking. Linguists call them deictic words, from the Greek for pointing. Eu points at the speaker, você at the person addressed, hoje at the day of speaking, aqui at the speaker's place. When a statement is reported, the situation is now the reporter's, so these words must be re-pointed to keep referring to the same people, day and place. English does this too (I becomes she, tomorrow becomes the next day, here becomes there), so the habit is familiar.

For persons, ask who is speaking now and to whom. Ela disse: Eu te amo, said to me and retold by me, becomes Ela disse que me amava: eu was she, so the verb goes to the third person singular, and te (you) was me. If I retell it to someone else, the object becomes ele: Ela disse que amava ele, or in formal writing que o amava. Possessives follow the same rule: meu carro, said by Paulo, becomes o carro dele, with dele or dela (of him, of her) as in the unit on possessives.

Time words are counted from the original moment of speaking rather than from the reporter's now. Hoje, the day of speaking, becomes naquele dia; ontem becomes na véspera or no dia anterior; amanhã becomes no dia seguinte; agora becomes naquele momento or então; semana que vem becomes na semana seguinte; and há dois dias becomes dois dias antes. Naquele is the contraction of em and aquele. The demonstrative aquele points at what is far from the speaker, and here it is far away in time. Place words follow the same step: aqui becomes ali or lá, and este becomes aquele. None of this is needed when the report is made on the same day and in the same place: Ele disse que vem amanhã is correct if he said it today.

An indirect question is a question told inside a statement. It has no question mark, because it does not ask anything now. A yes or no question has no question word, and the report adds se: Você quer café? becomes Ela perguntou se eu queria café. An open question keeps its question word: Onde você mora? becomes Ela perguntou onde eu morava. English must rearrange the word order and drop do (Where do you live? becomes where I lived), whereas Portuguese direct questions already use statement order, so the order stays as it was and only the pronouns and tenses change. The se of reported questions is the same word as the se of conditions (se chover, if it rains); English uses whether, or if, for the reported question and if for the condition.

grammar.title: Formal backshift versus the colloquial present
grammar.explanation:
The system of the previous notes is the standard of writing: journalism, reports, minutes and careful speech. It anchors every report to the original moment, so a reader who was not there can tell what came before what. Spoken Brazilian Portuguese relaxes it for a good reason. When the reporter and the listener share the situation, the context already says when things happen, and the original tense is often still true. People therefore keep the tense of the original words: Ele falou que vem amanhã, Ela disse que tá cansada, O chefe avisou que a reunião é às dez. Nobody will consider this incorrect, and a fully shifted sentence in casual chat can sound stiff.

Other colloquial habits follow the same preference for simplicity. Falar que is at least as frequent as dizer que in speech. Storytelling uses the frame aí ele falou, aí eu falei, or even just aí ele: não vou, where aí means then and the quote follows. The preterite often replaces the pluperfect: Disse que foi ao médico instead of que tinha ido. Requests replace the imperfect subjunctive with pedir pra gente plus an infinitive: Ela pediu pra gente esperar. Pra is the spoken form of para, and a gente, we, is the subject of esperar; the written equivalents are pediu que esperássemos or pediu para esperarmos. An unknown or unimportant agent is expressed by the third person plural with no pronoun: Falou que cancelaram a reunião.

A reporting verb in the present never causes a shift, because the reporter's moment is the moment being reported: Ela diz que está cansada, Ele está dizendo que vai chegar tarde. This is also why headlines are in the present (Ministro diz que vai aumentar o imposto) and why a text can say O relatório informa que as vendas cresceram: a document speaks for as long as it exists.

As an advanced learner, aim to control both registers. Shift the tenses when you write minutes, summarize a meeting by email or speak formally; use the lighter forms with friends. What must be right in both registers is the logic: pronouns and time words point at the right people and moments, and a request or suggestion is kept apart from a statement of fact.

culture.title: Disse me disse, rádio corredor e áudios do WhatsApp
culture.text:
Brazilians have a vivid vocabulary for passing on information. A fofoca is gossip, and the expression disse me disse, literally said-me-said, describes the tangle of versions that follows any rumor. In offices, the informal network of rumors is called rádio corredor, literally radio corridor. The children's game that English speakers call telephone is telefone sem fio, telephone without wire, and it is the standard image for how a message changes as it passes from person to person. People also protect their sources with ouvi dizer, I heard it said, which announces that what follows is hearsay.

In daily life, reporting is often delivered in the middle of a long story. Brazilians love to tell what happened in detail, recreating dialogues with aí ele falou, aí eu falei. On messaging apps, people send long voice messages, called áudios, and later summarize them for others: A Carla mandou um áudio dizendo que vai atrasar. It is common to ask Me resume o áudio?, meaning Can you summarize the audio for me?, when a message is too long to listen to. Learning to summarize is therefore a practical skill, not only an academic one.

In the press and in official life, reported speech follows strict conventions. Newspapers use segundo, de acordo com and fontes to attribute statements, and many headlines put the verb in the present: Ministro diz que vai aumentar o imposto. A press conference is an entrevista coletiva, literally a collective interview, usually shortened to a coletiva. Companies and public bodies record meetings in an ata, written in the third person and in the past: O diretor declarou que..., A secretária sugeriu que... If you work in Brazil, you will probably read, and sometimes write, such a text.

paragraphs.target: Na sexta-feira passada, dona Célia pediu para a filha avisar o irmão de que o almoço de domingo seria às duas da tarde, e não à noite, como no mês anterior.
paragraphs.source: Last Friday, dona Célia asked her daughter to tell her brother that Sunday's lunch would be at two in the afternoon, and not in the evening, as in the previous month.
paragraphs.source_literal: In-the sixth-fair passed, lady Célia asked for the daughter to-notify the brother of that the lunch of Sunday would-be at-the two of-the afternoon, and not at-the night, like in-the month previous.

paragraphs.source: The daughter, Renata, was in traffic and sent her brother a voice message saying that their mother had said that the lunch was at two. There was a lot of honking in the background.

paragraphs.target: O irmão, o Paulo, só ouviu o áudio à noite e entendeu que o almoço seria às três. Comentou com a esposa que a mãe tinha marcado para as três, e ela disse que faria uma sobremesa.
paragraphs.source: The brother, Paulo, only listened to the message at night and understood that lunch would be at three. He mentioned to his wife that his mother had set it for three, and she said she would make a dessert.
paragraphs.source_literal: The brother, the Paulo, only heard the audio at-the night and understood that the lunch would-be at-the three. Commented with the wife that the mother had marked for the three, and she said that would-do a dessert.

paragraphs.target: No domingo, Paulo chegou à casa da mãe às três e encontrou todo mundo já à mesa. A mãe perguntou por que ele tinha se atrasado, e ele respondeu que a Renata tinha avisado que seria às três.
paragraphs.source: On Sunday, Paulo arrived at his mother's house at three and found everybody already at the table. His mother asked why he was late, and he answered that Renata had told him it would be at three.
paragraphs.source_literal: In-the Sunday, Paulo arrived at-the house of-the mother at-the three and found all world already at-the table. The mother asked for what he had himself delayed, and he answered that the Renata had notified that would-be at-the three.

paragraphs.target: A Renata jurou que tinha dito duas horas. Ela ouviu o áudio no celular do irmão, e todos reconheceram que a palavra podia mesmo ser confundida por causa do barulho.
paragraphs.source: Renata swore that she had said two o'clock. She listened to the message on her brother's phone, and everyone admitted that the word could really be mistaken because of the noise.
paragraphs.source_literal: The Renata swore that had said two hours. She heard the audio in-the cellphone of-the brother, and all recognized that the word could same be confused by cause of-the noise.

paragraphs.target: Dona Célia riu e falou que, da próxima vez, ia ligar ela mesma. Paulo prometeu que daria mais atenção aos recados, e todos concordaram que a sobremesa chegou na hora certa.
paragraphs.source: Dona Célia laughed and said that next time she would call herself. Paulo promised that he would pay more attention to messages, and everyone agreed that the dessert arrived at exactly the right time.

questions.prompt: What did dona Célia ask Renata to do?
choices: To tell her brother the lunch would be at two
questions.explanation: Dona Célia pediu para a filha avisar o irmão sobre o horário do almoço.

questions.prompt: Why did Paulo misunderstand the time?
choices: The message was in writing and had a typo
His wife told him the wrong time
questions.explanation: Havia muito barulho de buzina ao fundo, so the time was heard as three.

questions.prompt: What happened when Paulo arrived on Sunday?
choices: Everybody was already at the table
questions.explanation: He chegou às três e encontrou todo mundo já à mesa.

questions.prompt: What did dona Célia say she would do next time?
questions.explanation: She said that, da próxima vez, ia ligar ela mesma. Ia plus infinitive is the imperfect of ir, the future seen from the past.

questions.prompt: In Renata's message, 'a mãe tinha falado que o almoço era às duas' contains two tenses. What does tinha falado show about the order of events?
choices: Dona Célia spoke before Renata sent the message
Both happened at exactly the same moment
questions.explanation: Tinha plus a participle is the pluperfect, the past of a past: the mother's speaking came before the moment of Renata's message.

exercises.prompt: Why does 'Estou cansado' become 'estava cansado' in 'Ele disse que estava cansado'?
choices: Because que always forces the imperfect
Because the reporter looks back from a later moment, so the speaker's present is reported as a past state
Because the speaker was not sure
exercises.explanation: A tense places an event relative to a reference moment. Retold later, the speaker's present is past, and the imperfect is the tense of past states.

exercises.prompt: Choose the formal report of: Ela disse: 'Fui ao médico.'
choices: Ela disse que ia ao médico.
Ela disse que iria ao médico.
Ela disse que tinha ido ao médico.
Ela disse que fosse ao médico.
exercises.explanation: An action before the original moment, expressed by the preterite, becomes the pluperfect: tinha plus the participle ido.

exercises.prompt: In the formal system, which form replaces the future of 'Chegarei cedo' after 'Ele disse que'?
exercises.explanation: The conditional is the future seen from the past, so the future shifts to it.

exercises.prompt: Ela disse: 'Eu te amo.' She said it to me, and I am retelling it. Which report is correct?
exercises.explanation: Te meant the person addressed, who is now the reporter, so it becomes me. Eu was the speaker, so the verb goes to the third person.

exercises.prompt: In which sentence does the reporting verb itself prevent any shift of tense?
exercises.explanation: With a reporting verb in the present, the reporter's moment is still the moment of speaking, so nothing moves back.

exercises.prompt: Why does 'Ela pediu que eu esperasse' use the subjunctive?
choices: Because the sentence is in the past
Because pedir reports a request, something wished for and not yet real, and the past verb makes it the imperfect subjunctive
Because que is always followed by the subjunctive
exercises.explanation: The subjunctive marks what is wished for rather than asserted. After dizer que a fact follows and the indicative is used.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'He denied having said that' when the same person denies and did the saying?
exercises.explanation: With the same subject, negar takes an infinitive, here the perfect infinitive ter dito. With que the verb would need the subjunctive: negou que tivesse dito.

exercises.prompt: Why does 'Ela perguntou se eu queria café' need the word se?
choices: Because the original yes or no question had no question word, and such a question is reported with se, whether
exercises.explanation: Que introduces statements; se introduces yes or no questions. Open questions keep their question word instead.

exercises.prompt: Why does a report say 'no dia seguinte' instead of 'amanhã' for a day after a past statement?
choices: Because amanhã counts from the moment of speaking now, while the reported day is counted from the original day
Because ia viajar is a past tense
exercises.explanation: Words that point at the speaker's situation must be re-pointed when the situation changes.
The n stands for em, as in no (em plus o) and na (em plus a). Naquele dia is in that day.

exercises.prompt: Why does véspera carry an accent?
choices: It is stressed on the third to last syllable, and a word stressed that far back is always accented
exercises.explanation: The defaults only cover stress on the last or the second to last syllable. VÉS-pe-ra breaks both, so the accent is required.

exercises.prompt: Why does 'você' carry a circumflex while 'falou' carries no accent?
choices: Você breaks the default for words ending in e, and the closed e takes the circumflex; falou ends in u, which already predicts last-syllable stress
exercises.explanation: An accent is written only when stress departs from the default of the ending.

exercises.prompt: What is the literal rendering of 'ouvir dizer' in 'tinha ouvido dizer que ele estava procurando outro emprego'?
exercises.explanation: Literally to hear say. The natural English is to hear it said, or to hear that: information that reached you second hand.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence sounds most natural in casual conversation?
choices: Ela declarara que viria no dia seguinte.
Ela afirmou que viria no dia seguinte.
Ela disse que viesse no dia seguinte.
exercises.explanation: Speech keeps the original present after falou que. Declarara is the literary pluperfect ending in -ra, afirmou que viria is formal, and disse que viesse is wrong because a statement of fact takes the indicative.

exercises.prompt_target: Ela contou que ___ morando em Recife.
exercises.hint_source: She said she was living in Recife.
exercises.explanation: In the formal system the present progressive shifts to the imperfect progressive; everyday speech can keep está.

exercises.prompt_target: Ela disse que já ___ enviado o relatório.
exercises.hint_source: She said she had already sent the report.
exercises.explanation: The pluperfect is the imperfect of ter (or haver) plus the participle enviado.

exercises.prompt_target: Ele prometeu que ___ no dia seguinte.
exercises.hint_source: He promised he would come back the next day.
exercises.explanation: A promise looks forward, so the future shifts to the conditional or to ia plus the infinitive.

exercises.prompt_target: Eles disseram que ___ ali desde o dia anterior.
exercises.hint_source: They said they had been there since the day before.
exercises.explanation: Ali and o dia anterior show the formal system, so the present estão shifts to the imperfect estavam.

exercises.prompt_target: Ele disse que, quando ___ ao hotel, ligaria para a família.
exercises.hint_source: He said that when he arrived at the hotel, he would call the family.
exercises.explanation: The future subjunctive of the original (quando eu chegar) becomes the imperfect subjunctive after a past reporting verb.

exercises.prompt_target: Ela me perguntou ___ eu já tinha almoçado.
exercises.hint_source: She asked me whether I had already had lunch.
exercises.explanation: A yes or no question has no question word, so the report introduces it with se.

exercises.hint_source: She asked me to wait there.
exercises.explanation: The imperative Espere aqui! becomes an imperfect subjunctive after pedir que, and aqui becomes ali.

exercises.prompt_target: A diretora sugeriu que todos ___ mais cedo.
exercises.hint_source: The director suggested that everybody arrive earlier.
exercises.explanation: Sugerir que proposes an action that has not happened, so the imperfect subjunctive follows: eles chegaram gives chegassem.

exercises.hint_source: He denied having read the message.
exercises.explanation: Negar que takes the subjunctive, because the denied claim is not asserted. Tivesse lido is the counterpart of tinha lido.

exercises.prompt_target: Ele disse que ia viajar ___ dia seguinte.
exercises.hint_source: He said he was going to travel the next day.
exercises.explanation: Em plus o contracts to no: no dia seguinte, in the following day.

exercises.prompt_target: O policial mandou o motorista ___ o carro.
exercises.hint_source: The police officer ordered the driver to stop the car.
exercises.explanation: Mandar in the sense of to order takes an object plus an infinitive.
The formal system shifts the present to the imperfect; everyday speech can keep the present.

exercises.prompt_source: She asked me whether I was coming.
answers: Ela perguntou se eu ia vir.

exercises.explanation: A yes or no question is reported with se, and você becomes eu because the reporter is the person who was addressed.

exercises.explanation: Prometer looks forward: conditional, ia plus infinitive, or a plain infinitive with the same subject.

answers: Eles pediram para a gente esperar.

exercises.prompt_source: She said that she loved me.
exercises.explanation: Te in the original words becomes me, since the person addressed is now the reporter; amo becomes amava in the formal system.
